scope: Persisted content-transport stop checks; offline candidate only, not global application acceptance

contract.autochat: bot_running is the existing AUTOMATION master/kill switch. Automatic worker content sends and all six LLM paths re-read committed bot_running immediately before each request. Only JSON true enables automatic content. Explicit manual approvals and manual analysis remain available while automation is paused; they still require a valid non-archived owner in multi-character mode. No AutoPost switch is silently applied to AutoChat.
contract.autopost: global_pause stops publication and automatic planning. dry_run suppresses publication, NOT generation/processing. The automatic generate_plan entry carries a context through awaited LLM work; each initial/reasoning-retry/fallback LLM request checks fresh persisted owner runtime. Manual generation/translation/description tools and explicit short setup completion tests remain usable during publication pause.
contract.ownership: Content clients reject missing, unknown or archived character owners in multi-character mode. Synchronous AutoChat validation supports file-backed SQLite AutoPost owner registry only; unsupported synchronous backends fail closed. Existing authentication is unchanged.
contract.claims: Definitely blocked sends remain pending, unscheduled, auto_send=0, retain operator edits and have a static sanitized error. Interrupted pending OR approved claims are released to pending manual review, never auto-rescheduled. Successful sent drafts are not relabeled.
contract.race_limit: Fresh read before I/O, not a distributed DB/HTTP transaction. A stop cannot recall an already transmitted request or eliminate the final read/send interval. Concurrent in-flight ownership/archive races cannot be made atomic with provider transport.

limitations: No new universal cross-module emergency-stop setting or UI. AutoPost publication pause does not mute AutoChat manual approval, manual content tools, setup/auth refresh or operator notifications.

AutoPost persistent transport checks are opt-in multi-character behavior, matching existing architecture; legacy AutoPost mode retains existing settings semantics. AutoChat automatic master checks also work in legacy file-backed mode.

Direct internal calls to automatic routines outside their real worker/job entry context must explicitly carry the automatic scope. Existing HTTP/manual analysis and preview proposal generation intentionally remain manual/read-only flows.
Shared task/thread architecture is preserved. No cross-process barriers, concurrent HTTP cancellation, OS-crash or live worker/scheduler acceptance is claimed.
Synchronous AutoChat owner validation fails closed for non-file SQLite and PostgreSQL; no synchronous PostgreSQL bridge was introduced.
Six-character matrices use real send/client functions and synthetic file stores, not six-character UI/startup/provider-account acceptance.
Remaining settings/UI/package/review acceptance and six known baseline failures still block deployment.
